---

## 3. Facts

1. The Complainant is a consumer within the meaning of Section 2(7) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, having purchased a flight ticket from the Opposite Party (airline) for personal travel, not for any commercial purpose or resale.

2. On or around [TO CONFIRM – March 2026], the Complainant purchased a flight ticket from the Opposite Party for a consideration of **₹18,000** (Rupees Eighteen Thousand only). The ticket details, including flight number, date of travel, and invoice/booking reference, are as follows: [TO CONFIRM].

3. The cause of action arose on **01 March 2026**, when the Opposite Party cancelled the said flight.

4. Following cancellation of the flight by the Opposite Party, the Complainant duly requested a full refund of ₹18,000.

5. The Opposite Party has, without lawful justification, refused to process or issue the said refund to the Complainant.

6. The Complainant has made repeated attempts to resolve the matter through [TO CONFIRM – calls, emails, written correspondence], all of which have failed. Details of such correspondence are annexed hereto.

7. The Complainant has suffered financial loss of ₹18,000 and consequential hardship, inconvenience and mental agony due to the conduct of the Opposite Party.

---

## 4. Deficiency in Service

The conduct of the Opposite Party amounts to a clear **deficiency in service** within the meaning of Section 2(11) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, in that:

(a) The Opposite Party unilaterally cancelled the flight for which the Complainant had paid full consideration;

(b) Despite cancellation being entirely attributable to the Opposite Party, it has wrongfully withheld the refund of ₹18,000 due and payable to the Complainant;

(c) The Opposite Party has failed to perform its service obligations in the manner contracted and has thereby caused quantifiable loss and suffering to the Complainant.

The Complainant's right to seek redressal is protected under Section 2(9) of the Act.

---

## 5. Relief Sought

In view of the facts and circumstances stated above, the Complainant most respectfully prays that this Hon'ble District Commission be pleased to direct the Opposite Party to:

(a) **Refund** the ticket amount of **₹18,000** (Rupees Eighteen Thousand only) along with interest at the rate of [TO CONFIRM] % per annum from 01 March 2026 till realisation;

(b) Pay **compensation** of ₹[TO CONFIRM] towards mental agony, harassment and inconvenience caused to the Complainant;

(c) Pay **costs of litigation** as the Hon'ble Commission deems fit;

(d) Pass such other and further orders as this Hon'ble Commission deems just and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case.

*(Reliefs under Section 39 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.)*

---

## 6. Sections Relied Upon

| Section | Title | Relevance |
|---|---|---|
| 2(7) | Consumer | Complainant qualifies as a consumer |
| 2(11) | Deficiency | Airline's refusal to refund constitutes deficiency in service |
| 2(9) | Consumer Rights | Right to redressal for the Complainant |
| 34 | Jurisdiction of District Commission | Pecuniary and territorial jurisdiction |
| 35 | Manner of filing complaint | Complaint filed by consumer before District Commission |
| 38 | Procedure on admission of complaint | Governing procedure for hearing |
| 39 | Reliefs | Basis for refund, compensation and costs prayed |
| 69 | Limitation period | Complaint filed within 2 years of cause of action (01 March 2026) |

---

## 7. Documents Annexed

1. ID proof of Complainant
2. Proof of purchase – flight ticket invoice / booking confirmation [TO CONFIRM: booking reference]
3. Warranty/guarantee card, if any
4. Correspondence with Opposite Party (emails, letters, screenshots of chats/calls)
5. Proof of amount paid – bank statement / payment receipt showing debit of ₹18,000
6. Notice sent to Opposite Party, if any
7. [Any cancellation notice or communication received from the airline – implied by facts]

---

## 8. Verification
